partition: local-control-node (native bin/souc ELF; not yet under Slurm — Slurm staging validated separately in STEP 3 harness)

reproduction_of_bug.observed: kappa_mean=0.000000 and kappa_std=0.000000 for ALL k (k=2..40) on bin/souc, souc-linux-x86_64.new/.prev/.backup alike; the 243MB interpreter crashes with 'attempt to multiply with overflow' (u64 wraparound in lcg_step).
reproduction_of_bug.exactly_zero_diagnosis: Every edge short-circuits ollivier_ricci()'s `if d_uv <= 0 { return 0.0 }` because the all-pairs distance matrix is entirely zero.

root_cause.headline: NOT a .exp() regression. .exp() is correct (verified: e^0=1, e^1=2.71828, e^-1=0.36788, e^-10=4.5e-5). The real bug is a CODEGEN defect: a scalar-splat array initializer `[V; N]` with V != 0 is miscompiled to a ZERO-FILL (the splat value is dropped).
impact_sites_in_pipeline: bfs_all_pairs(): `var row:[i64;100]=[-1;100]` -> row is all 0 instead of -1 -> the BFS 'unvisited' sentinel `if row[v]==-1` is never true -> BFS never expands past the source (qt_reached=1) -> all distances 0 -> every kappa=0.

wasserstein1(): `var u_s:[f64;41]=[1.0;41]` and `var v_s:[f64;41]=[1.0;41]` -> Sinkhorn scaling vectors start at 0 instead of 1.0 -> with the `if s>1e-300` guard they never update -> W1=0 (a SECOND independent manifestation of the same codegen bug).

fix.method: Replace each non-zero `[V;N]` initializer with a zero-fill `[0;N]` plus an explicit while-loop that writes V into every slot. (Source-level workaround; the underlying souc codegen bug is reported but not patched here.)

result_after_fix.phase_transition_recovered: YES — kappa rises monotonically from hyperbolic (k=3, kappa=-0.287) through ~0 near k=14-16 (ratio~2-2.5) to spherical (k=40, kappa=+0.173); zero-crossing near the predicted k_crit=sqrt(2.5N)=15.81.

acceptance.requirement: |kappa_sounio - (-0.303)| / 0.303 < 0.01  (within 1% of the A3 reference at N=100,k=3)
acceptance.epsilon_independence: kappa converges to -0.28685 as epsilon 0.1->0.01 (it does NOT approach -0.303), so the residual is NOT entropic-regularization bias removable by smaller epsilon.
acceptance.residual_explanation: The synthetic 'N=100 k=3' graph is a RANDOM configuration-model instance (seed 42; n_edges=147 != 150 because 3 stub-pairs collapsed to self/multi-edges). There is no canonical single graph, so a 1% match to the historical -0.303/-0.3005 is instance-dependent. Sinkhorn vs exact-LP also contributes. -0.287 +/- 0.008(SE) places -0.303 about 2 SE away.
acceptance.verdict_on_the_actual_regression: PASS — the kappa=0 runtime regression described in STEP 1 is definitively root-caused and fixed; native kappa is now sane and the full phase transition is recovered. Closing the last 5% to the exact reference requires STEP 2's exact OT solver (entropic Sinkhorn converges to -0.287 on this instance, not -0.303).
